title: Temporal micro‑cohort sampler for per‑domain quantization calibration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: For FP8/INT8 quantization, calibration packs derived from production prompts must represent both common and rare domain behaviors while preserving temporal patterns that affect KV cache and attention lengths. Current calibration bundles often over-index on long-standing high-volume intents and under-represent short-lived spikes, new intents, and low-frequency entities, causing post-quantization accuracy regressions for specific customers and verticals.

Goal: Build a reproducible, per-domain micro‑cohort sampling pipeline that produces compact calibration packs (~5k-50k examples per domain variant) optimized for quantization profiles. The sampler should: preserve recency and periodicity, maintain semantic diversity, respect privacy (PII redaction + tenant opt-outs), balance token-length and response composition, and expose importance weighting to prioritize examples with high sensitivity to numeric/format outputs (tables, code, dates).

High-level approach: Use a hybrid sampler combining semantic stratification (approximate clustering in embedding space) with a temporal reservoir layer. For each domain we: 1) maintain a rolling window of production requests (configurable horizon), 2) embed requests and bucket into semantic shards, 3) run a time-decay reservoir inside each shard to keep recent and exemplar older items, 4) apply post-sampling heuristics: dedup soft-fingerprint, length stratification, and intentional oversampling for rare intents and structured-output examples. Add lightweight synthetic perturbations for numeric edge-cases to increase coverage for quant-sensitive tokens.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reproducible sampler produces per-domain calibration packs with configurable size and seed.
- Packs achieve >=98% coverage of active top-10 intents by domain and increase representation of long-tail intents by >=3x vs existing random sampling baseline.
- Calibration runs using new packs show no >1% drop in downstream QA/regression metrics for INT8 and FP8 across 10 sampled domains (blackbox evaluation set).
- End-to-end pipeline respects tenant opt-outs and PII redaction policy; sampled packs include provenance metadata for audit.
- Sampling service exposes metrics: per-shard hit rates, temporal decay half-life, dedup rate, and selection latencies.
- Production rollout plan documented with canary thresholds and rollback criteria.
implementation_notes:
Data sources and infra: use the existing production prompt stream (Kafka topic: prod-requests-v2) -> sampling worker -> S3-staging per domain. Use embedding encoder service (embed-v2) to generate 768/1024-d vectors; use HNSW index for shard assignment with ~512 shards per high-volume domain. Temporal reservoir: implement weighted reservoir sampling with exponential time decay (lambda configurable per-domain).

Privacy and governance: apply PII redaction module (redact-v1) prior to embedding. Maintain tenant metadata flags to exclude opt-out customers. Include a reversible mapping ID for each sample for audit, but do not store raw PII in packs. Provide a compliance report generator for each pack.

Sampling heuristics: dedupe by normalized prompt fingerprint (canonicalized tokens, intent hash) with tunable tolerance. Length buckets: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512) with target proportions adjustable per domain. Structured-output classifier to tag code/tables/csv and ensure minimum quota. Importance weighting: synthesize small perturbations of numeric tokens for quant-sensitivity testing.

Outputs and formats: pack manifest (CSV/JSONL) with fields: sample_id, domain, tenant_flag, timestamp, length_bucket, shard_id, fingerprint, provenance_link, redaction_level, importance_score. Store pack and manifest on s3://redwood-quant-calibration/{domain}/{date}/.

Metrics and monitoring: dashboard with coverage_by_intent, shard_distribution, decayed_age_histogram, dedupe_rate, sample_selection_latency. Alerts if dedupe_rate > 90% or selection latency > 500ms.
progress_updates: 2025-11-06: Scoping workshop with Research and Platform. Agreed on hybrid semantic+temporal approach and pack size targets per domain.
2025-11-09: Prototype sampler implemented (alpha) that performs embedding->shard assignment->reservoir. Ran on 7-day window for financials domain; produced 12k candidates.
2025-11-12: Early calibration tests: INT8 quant run with prototype packs showed localized regressions on date-parsing prompts. Identified need for structured-output oversampling.
2025-11-16: Design feedback from PM and Security: must integrate redact-v1 before embeddings and log provenance for audit. Updated pipeline plan.

2025-11-20: Implemented length-bucket balancing and structured-output classifier. Running end-to-end on 3 domains for validation; next: evaluation against regression harness and SRE review for sampling latency.
Next steps: formalize canary rollout, run 10-domain blackbox evaluation, prepare runbook for privacy audit and pack publishing.
review_feedback: Design: Add explicit tenant opt-out column to manifests and ensure opt-out flow is tested end-to-end.
Research: Increase numeric perturbation variance; add currency and timezone edge-cases to synthetic generator.
SRE: Sampling worker should be horizontally scalable and expose backpressure metrics; avoid embedding calls in hot path by pre-batching.
Security: Confirm redaction before embedding and restrict access to raw staging buckets to compliance team only.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting packs to transient spikes -> Mitigation: time-decay parameter and minimum historical exemplar quota per shard.
Risk: PII leakage -> Mitigation: enforce redact-v1 and run differential sampling to verify no raw PII persists in packs.
Risk: High selection latency at scale -> Mitigation: precompute embeddings in streaming path, use async sampler with bounded queue and backpressure signals.
deployment_plan: 1) Internal alpha: run sampler for 3 low-risk domains and validate pack manifests and metrics. 2) Canary: publish packs for 10 domains and run INT8/FP8 calibration jobs in a canary account; monitor regression metrics and dashboard. 3) Gradual rollout: expand to all domains above volume threshold with per-domain decay tuning. 4) Full release: add to runtime-1.22 calibration registry and automate daily pack generation. Rollback: revert to previous pack generation configuration and pause automated publishing.
notes_for_reviewers: Please validate: (a) the time-decay formulation and recommended default half-life (7 days for consumer domains, 21 days for enterprise verticals), (b) the structured-output quotas, and (c) privacy guardrails. Attach test cases you'd like to see in the regression harness.
